note: Valid header sections: what a sender writes in core deterministic encoding, and encodings a receiver accepts although a sender never writes them.

cases.note: A header with no entries is the empty map a0. A frame with no header at all has HeaderLength 0 instead (spec 5.2).
Integer keys in ascending order: 1 and 2 encode as 01 and 02.
10 (0a) sorts before -1 (20): keys are ordered by their encoded bytes, and the major type is in the first byte.
"b" (61 62) sorts before "aa" (62 61 61): the length in the head byte is compared first.
Keys of four major types sort by their first byte: unsigned, negative, byte string, text string.
Each value uses the shortest head: 24 needs one extra byte, 256 two, 65536 four, 2^32 eight.
Each float uses the shortest width that keeps its exact value: 1.5 in f16, 100000.0 in f32, 0.1 in f64.
Key order applies to every map, including one nested inside a value.
Depth 16, the default limit: the map is depth 1 and holds 15 nested arrays.
A 7-byte header against a 7-byte limit is accepted: the limit is inclusive.
1 in a two-byte head (18 01). Receivers accept it; a sender writes 01.
1.5 as an f64. Receivers accept it; a sender writes the f16 f9 3e 00.
Key 2 before key 1. Receivers accept it; a sender sorts the keys.
